title: Cycle Length Queries in a Tree
summary: Given an integer n, consider a complete binary tree with 2^n - 1 nodes.
statement: Given an integer n, consider a complete binary tree with 2^n - 1 nodes. Each node with value val has a left child with value 2 * val and a right child with value 2 * val + 1. For each query, add an edge between nodes ai and bi, find the cycle length, then remove the edge. Return an array where each element is the cycle length for the corresponding query.
constraints: Nodes 1 through 2^n-1 form the implicit complete binary tree with parent floor(node/2).
For each query, temporarily add one edge between its two nodes.
Return the resulting cycle length, including the added edge, for each query.
hints: The cycle is the existing tree path plus the added edge.
Repeatedly move the larger node label to its parent; in this heap labeling it is always at least as deep as the smaller current label.
Count one for the added edge and one for every parent move until the nodes meet.
The meeting node is their LCA and the parent moves count the exact tree-path edges, so the total is the cycle length.
editorial: The meeting node is their LCA and the parent moves count the exact tree-path edges, so the total is the cycle length.

tests.explanation: Tree-path distances are three, four, and two; including the added edge gives [4,5,3].
The tree edge path from one to three has length one, so adding the same connection forms a two-edge cycle by the query definition.
